examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Check mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait. Prevention breaks a necessary condition; avoidance such as Banker's algorithm checks safety before grants. With single-instance resource types, a wait-for cycle characterizes deadlock; with multiple instances, cycles alone need not suffice. Unsafe is not the same as already deadlocked.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Six processes each need at most 3 identical resource instances, requesting one at a time. What minimum supply guarantees absence of resource deadlock?

**Answer: 13.** At most six processes can each hold two without any being able to finish, using 6·(3−1)=12 instances. One additional instance lets a process obtain its maximum and finish, releasing resources. The guarantee is 12+1=13.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The guarantee assumes every process eventually releases resources after completing and has no other blocking dependency. Resource-count bounds do not prevent unrelated protocol deadlocks.

Unsafe and deadlocked are not synonyms.
